verdicts.summary: I tried a transient exit 128, old git echoing --path-format, newline paths, an unborn HEAD, non-UTF8 output and the retry/fsync hooks. None gives a wrong result. Every malformed or unexpected output falls back to the old separate commands.
evidence: apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:852-869 — exit 0 needs exactly 4 lines and exit 1 exactly 3, with a trailing empty line. Old git adds a line and a newline path adds at least one, so both fail the count and fall back. Exit 0 and exit 1 expect different counts, so they cannot be confused.

apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:865-869 — any other exit code (such as 128) goes to resolveGitCommonDir, which throws as before outside a repo. hasHeadCommit already treated any non-zero exit as no HEAD (793-800), so a transient 128 gives the same answer as before.
apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:940-948 — when indexPath is undefined, the old inline `rev-parse --git-path index` still runs, so the fallback path reads the index path the same way as before.

apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:279-298 and 304 — the darwin fsync retry and the non-zero exit error both need !allowNonZeroExit. The new call sets allowNonZeroExit, and a plain rev-parse has no fsync args anyway.

apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:349-367 — the capture retry only matches retryable VcsProcessExitError, which cannot occur with allowNonZeroExit. The fallback calls use different operation labels, so they are unchanged.

apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:521-555 — gitCommand adds only `-C cwd` and sets no env override. GIT_INDEX_FILE is not set for this call, so `--git-path index` resolves the user's real index as before.

apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:819-831 — the old code resolved a relative common dir against the real cwd. `--path-format=absolute` on git 2.31+ gives an absolute path, and the result is trimmed as before. Non-UTF8 paths had the same exposure in the old code.
